subject: Evaluation acceptance protocol & rollback harbor
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jim Carter <jim.carter@medipulse.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Dec 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Evaluation acceptance protocol & rollback harbor

Hi Jim —

Thanks again for the time this morning. Per our discussion I’m attaching a lightweight mutual action plan (MAP) and an evidence template we typically use to validate acceptance criteria during an evaluation.

Goal: agree on the success signals and explicit exit gates so both teams have a clear path-to-close and a tested rollback if we need to revert.

What I’m proposing in this first pass:
- Acceptance tests grouped by capability (latency, throughput, functional correctness, security/compliance artifacts)
- Owner and due date for each test (MediPulse vs Redwood)
- Minimum pass thresholds and smoke-check scripts for quick validation
- Escape hatch / rollback triggers + operational playbook (included as a stub)

Attachments: MAP-v1.xlsx (mutual action plan), acceptance-evidence-template.docx (evidence checklist).

Ask: Can you confirm stakeholders I should include on the MAP and whether Procurement wants the MAP in DocuSign or a shared Drive folder? If Procurement prefers, I can route the MAP there and include the procurement SLA items.

If this looks fine I’ll loop in Priyom and Marcus to fill in technical owners and the rollback playbook details.

Best,
Sofia
Principal Solutions
Redwood Inference

From: Jim Carter <jim.carter@medipulse.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medipulse.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Evaluation acceptance protocol & rollback harbor

Sofia —

Appreciate the notes and attachments. Key stakeholder list below:
- Jim Carter (Dir, Product) — primary decision maker
- Maria Lopez (Eng manager) — technical owner
- Samir Patel (SRE) — will run smoke tests and help validate latency/throughput
- Procurement — procurement@medipulse.com (please include contract SLA items)

DocuSign preference: Procurement would like the MAP and the commercial addendum in the DocuSign route; technical attachments can live in a shared Drive. Could you put a short tracker line for the procurement SLA (credit for downtime, data residency confirmation) so Procurement can review?

Also: curious whether the rollback playbook assumes we keep traffic on our existing inference provider and run Redwood in parallel for a short canary, or if you expect a direct cutover for the evaluation. If you recommend parallel canary, outline the steps and timing.

Thanks — I’ll review the MAP and get Maria and Samir looped in.

—Jim
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jim Carter <jim.carter@medipulse.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@medipulse.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Dec 2025 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Evaluation acceptance protocol & rollback harbor

Team — forwarding Jim’s responses. Quick rundown of next steps for Redwood owners: please seed the MAP with technical owners, test owners, and the canary/rollback sequence. Procurement wants the commercial SLA line included for DocuSign.

I’ve linked the two attachments (MAP-v1.xlsx, acceptance-evidence-template.docx) — use them as the source-of-truth. Call out questions inline on the MAP.

Priority items:
1) Canary execution plan (parallel traffic vs cutover) — propose 48–72 hour canary window with metrics sampling and automated fallback if error rate > 1% or latency 2x baseline.
2) Acceptance thresholds for model outputs — need sample prompt set and 500-case concordance run.
3) Security artifacts — SOC 2 attestation summary, data retention confirmation, and audit log access (Samir will request an audit token).

Can we have an internal draft by EOD tomorrow so I can send the official MAP to Jim and Procurement?

Thanks,
Sofia

Date: Tue, 16 Dec 2025 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evaluation acceptance protocol & rollback harbor

Sofia / team —

I’ve populated MAP-v1.xlsx with owners, due dates and an initial set of acceptance tests. Highlights:
- Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms on redwood-dedicated region-us-west during a 60-minute steady-run (owner: Samir/Medipulse; validation: automated load harness)
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/min per instance with continuous batching (owner: Marcus/Redwood)
- Functional correctness: 500-case concordance against annotated prompt-set; pass if F1 > 0.85 (owner: Maria/Medipulse; assay: concordance script)
- Security: SOC2 summary and data retention TTL = 90 days (owner: Laura/Redwood)

Attached a small checklist and a draft rollback-playbook.pdf with trigger definitions. I marked the procurement SLA line for DocuSign.

Attachments referenced here: MAP-v1.xlsx (updated), acceptance-evidence-template.docx (filled), rollback-playbook.pdf (draft).

I’ll also include a short smoke script (bash + curl) for Samir to run during the canary.

—Priyom

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jim Carter <jim.carter@medipulse.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Dec 2025 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evaluation acceptance protocol & rollback harbor

Quick technical notes to add to the MAP:

- Canary plan: 2-phase parallel traffic test. Phase 1 (12 hours): 5% sampled traffic routed to Redwood with mirrored requests and output-only verification. Phase 2 (48 hours): 25% live traffic with active routing and automated trend detection.
- Failover triggers: immediate rollback if (a) error rate increases by > 0.5% sustained over 5 minutes, (b) model concordance drops > 7% vs baseline, or (c) verified data leakage indicator.
- Rollback mechanics: routing flip via load balancer (1-click), automated cache flush, and post-mortem checklist. Marcus will own the runbook and confirm runbook rehearse by Wed EOD.

I also added a short note recommending a dry-run of the smoke harness on staging prior to the live canary.

—Marcus
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Jim Carter <jim.carter@medipulse.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@medipulse.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Dec 2025 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Final MAP + acceptance evidence pack (request for sign-off)

Jim —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Attached is the updated MAP (MAP-v1.xlsx), the acceptance evidence template (acceptance-evidence-template.docx) filled with initial owners, and the rollback playbook PDF (rollback-playbook.pdf). Summary of critical items for your review and sign-off:

1) Acceptance gates (must pass all):
   - Latency (95p) < 350ms under test window
   - Functional concordance F1 >= 0.85 on 500-case set
   - No verified data-egress or PII exposure on sampled requests

2) Canary cadence: 12-hour mirror -> 48-hour 25% traffic -> full traffic (only after green checks)

3) Fail/rollback triggers: error-rate delta > 0.5% sustained over 5min OR concordance drop > 7% OR security indicator -> automatic rollback and troubleshooting cadence (see rollback-playbook.pdf)

4) Procurement items: commercial addendum line added in MAP (DocuSign route preferred).

Next steps after your sign-off:
- We’ll schedule a 30-min run-through with Maria and Samir to walk the smoke script and confirm Samir has the audit token.
- Procurement will receive the DocuSign packet with the MAP commercial row.
- Execution window proposal: Jan 6–8, 2026 for the canary (flexible).

Please reply with APPROVE or with changes by EOD Friday so we can lock dates and route DocuSign.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Sofia
Principal Solutions
Redwood Inference
